design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (workflow task), difficulty checking_fees_overdraft_and_disputes. Frozen 2026-08-28 15:20 EDT, a Friday and the account's cycle closing date (statement_cycle_day 28). Revision 3, after policy-task audit revision_2.

[0] Scope. This task claims three policies:
- checking_ext_transfer_fee_source_error_refund
- checking_ext_autopay_dispute_provisional_credit
- checking_ext_cycle_close_relationship_refund
It also claims the single workflow checking_wf_owed_credits_before_waiver_review and three tools: refund_transfer_fee_error_033d9cbf, post_dispute_provisional_credit_5453b90d, refund_same_day_maintenance_fee_e9518b99. Task 1 claims the other three policies and tools. The two scopes are disjoint and cover all six policies.

Blueprint blocker (T0-W1, unchanged). The only customer-owned events are the debit overdraft opt-in and account closure. The opt-in's owner_consent gate binds checking_account_id to a caller statement, which would put an internal uuid in the persona. Closure voids a same-day maintenance fee and has no cross-category numeric factor. So every workflow step is an agent posting, as the order_rationale states.

[1] Why it is a good test. The customer asks only whether today's 15.00 Interest Checking maintenance fee is right. At the opening it is right. The relationship balance is 1443.16 (checking) + 2847.30 (Goal Builder Savings 1159, active) + 10212.64 (12-Month Certificate 1903, active) = 14503.10, below the 15000.00 waiver_relationship_balance. The mortgage (182400.37) is excluded because Interest Checking has relationship_balance_includes_mortgage false. The ledger waivers (direct deposits, card purchases) are not_offered on this tier.

The root rule posts owed credits first, and the agent has to find them:
- (a) Two overdraft transfer fees of 10.00 (2026-07-20 and 2026-08-19). Each fee's own transfer (703.73 and 164.29) came from the Goal Builder Savings, whose tier has overdraft_protection_source_eligible false, so both fees are bank errors. The most recent is decided by the transfer-fee policy. The earlier one goes under base checking_evt_fee_refund, as the root rule says.
- (b) One submitted dispute (notice 2026-08-10, deadline 2026-08-24) on the 2026-08-05 PCB AUTO LOAN PMT debit of 972.40. The debit's counterparty is the New Vehicle Loan, whose autopay is enrolled from this checking with monthly_payment 486.20. The credit is min(972.40, 972.40, 972.40 - 486.20) = 486.20.
After these postings the relationship is 1949.36 + 2847.30 + 10212.64 = 15009.30, which meets 15000.00, so the fee is refunded.

[2] Problem-tree card. Root: checking_ext_cycle_close_relationship_refund, gate own_part.
- Edge 1 goes to checking_ext_transfer_fee_source_error_refund, kind value_input. policy_source: 'the refund of every overdraft transfer fee charged in error, the most recent one as checking_ext_transfer_fee_source_error_refund finds it and any earlier one under checking_evt_fee_refund'. False at opening: neither fee has a refund row.
- Edge 2 goes to checking_ext_autopay_dispute_provisional_credit, kind value_input. policy_source: 'the provisional credit that checking_ext_autopay_dispute_provisional_credit finds owed'. False at opening: the dispute is submitted and has no credit row.
- Order: fee refunds in posted order, then the credit (root rule).
- Sensitivity: skipping the refund tool (both fees) gives 14989.30, so the root refund becomes 0.00. Skipping only the earlier fee gives 14999.30 and 0.00. Skipping the credit gives 14523.10 and 0.00.
- Posting the credit first gives the same final hash.
- The persona names no prerequisite. The tools refuse nothing.

[3] Base-invariant card.
- The three refund calls carry every checking_fee_refund gate, because the contract inherits them all. These are courtesy gates, and they hold here too: codes eligible; fees posted on days 39, 9 and 0 of the 60-day window; one courtesy refund (2026-03-09), below the limit of 2; account active; no prior refund.
- checking_evt_electronic_dispute is policy_scope for refunds.
- The credit call: notice on day 5 of 120; credit_due on business day 10 = 2026-08-24; account opened 2019-05-06, so the 10-day deadline applies; status submitted; no credit yet.

[4] Business-object card. Every value is read from the object's own record:
- the fee's own amount;
- the fee's own transfer and that transfer's counterparty;
- the single dispute's own claimed_amount and disputed_txn_id;
- the disputed item's own counterparty, which identifies the loan.
Excluded: the 2026-07-06 autopay of 486.20 (the correct amount), the card purchases, payroll, and the February paper fee, which was already refunded once.

[5] Seed. Customer, checking account, and 22 ledger rows:
- payroll every other Friday;
- interest credits of 0.02, 0.04 and 0.02 on the cycle closing dates (0.01 APY band);
- both autopay debits, which name the auto loan as counterparty;
- two covered items with their transfers and fees;
- card purchases;
- the courtesy history;
- today's fee.
Also one dispute, savings, certificate, mortgage and auto loan. No maintenance fee posted for the June or July cycles because the relationship waiver was met at those closes, recomputed from the seed: at the 2026-06-28 close checking 4892.47 + savings 3715.32 (2847.30 today plus the two later transfers 164.29 and 703.73) + certificate 10212.64 = 18820.43; at the 2026-07-28 close checking 2130.04 (the 07-20 transfer brought the account to 0.00, the 10.00 fee to -10.00, payroll on 07-24 to 2130.00, interest 0.04) + savings 3011.59 (2847.30 plus the later 164.29 transfer) + certificate 10212.64 = 15354.27. Both are at or above 15000.00 even if one month's certificate compounding (about 32.77) is backed out. Interest rows in this seed are 0.02 (06-28), 0.04 (07-28) and 0.02 (08-28). The -10.00 dips after each transfer fee were cured within 4 and 2 days, so no extended fee or restriction is due.

[6] Persona (R2-T0-O1 addressed). The opening states today's $15.00 charge and her belief that she keeps plenty with the bank, with no figure. Any general question, including 'have you disputed anything', gets 'only calling about the fee today; please check the records'. That does not deny the claim on record, and there is no gap between branches. The August claim is confirmed only when the representative names it, without amount or date. 'Yes, please do' applies only to a correction the representative names.

[7] Standard solution. Reads: customer, verify (phone, DOB, SSN), checking, activity, disputes, savings, certificates, mortgage, auto loans. Writes in workflow order:
- refund the 2026-07-20 fee, 10.00, under base (step computed_by []);
- refund the 2026-08-19 fee, 10.00 (policy);
- post the credit, 486.20;
- refund the maintenance fee, 15.00.
Zero-wait: every input is an initial_state row or a synchronous earlier posting.

[8] Verification. check_compute --task 0 recomputes 10.00, 486.20 and 15.00 on the handling-time worlds, each equal to expected and gold. Forcing cross-category reads off changes every result. Zeroing history changes every result. A draft recomputation from the visible text alone gives the same writes.

[9] Revisions.
- Round 3, N1 (closed): the dispute policy now decides only an account with exactly one submitted dispute (compute submitted_count). With two or more submitted disputes, each credit is left to checking_evt_electronic_dispute alone. Whether the credit is owed is stated as the inherited deadline gate. The latest-first ordering sentence is removed, so no owed credit can be withheld. The world now has one dispute. The fourth workflow step became the earlier transfer fee, refunded under base with computed_by [], and the root rule names both fees.
- R2-O4 (closed): the de minimis and wrong-amount flags now require a fee to exist.
- R2-O5 (addressed, still an observation): the dispute rule now states the reading that an autopay payment PCB collects for its own loan is a transfer between the owner's PCB accounts and so names that loan as counterparty, and both autopay debits in the seed carry it. No overwrite is declared, because the field meaning ('The PCB account on the other side of an internal transfer, otherwise empty') sits in the base event definition, not in any base policy rule, and an overwrite can only supersede a policy-rule clause.
- R2-T0-W2 (addressed, still an observation): dataflow is [] again; the order_rationale explains that step 3 consumes the ledger balance, a side effect on the account record that no dataflow link can name.
- R2-T0-O1 (closed): a general question now gets 'only calling about the fee today; please check the records', which denies nothing on record.
- Ledger waivers (direct deposit, card purchases) were added to the root so it follows more of the base waiver set; both are not_offered on Interest Checking.
- Round 3 seed check: an earlier authoring note feared the July-cycle relationship fell below 15000.00; recomputation from the seed (see [5]) gives 15354.27, so no July fee is due and the world is consistent.
- Carried from rounds 1–2 as the auditor judged them: F1, F2, F3, F4, T0-C1, T0-O2, T0-O3, T0-O4, T0-O6, T0-O7, O3, O4, O5, O7 closed; O8 addressed; O6 withdrawn by the auditor (not a defect). T0-O5 (interest rows) remains closed with rows recomputed for this seed: 0.02, 0.04, 0.02 (the round-2 seed's August figure, 0.03, no longer applies). T0-W1 is not closed (blueprint blocker, see [0]).
- Re-run: all gates OK.

[10] Revision 4 (policy-KB / runtime-context audits, source-layer items). P1: the cycle-close policy's relationship-basis overwrite now carries, in its replaced_by and rule, the general sentence keeping checking_msr_relationship_balance for every relationship-balance determination outside this waiver review and the Private Client test, so the ordinary month-end waiver and the Private Client opening check keep their base basis. P3: the dispute policy's amount overwrite now covers every case: with two or more submitted disputes each amount stays the claimed_amount capped at the disputed item's amount; with exactly one submitted dispute the smallest-figure rule applies. P2 and P4 concern task 1's policies (see that task). Scored values unchanged: 10.00, 10.00, 486.20, 15.00; this world has exactly one submitted dispute.
user_scenario:
You are Deborah Ellison, a fifty-eight-year-old media specialist at a Greensboro middle school who has banked with Piedmont Crescent for years. You are calling on a Friday afternoon from your phone because this morning your banking app showed a $15.00 monthly service charge on your Interest Checking account ending 0736, dated today. You have never paid that charge before, and you are sure you keep plenty with the bank, between the checking, your Goal Builder savings and the twelve-month certificate you opened last fall, for it to be waived; you have never added the balances up yourself. What you want is simple: if that $15.00 should not have been charged, you want it put back on your checking today. You are not asking to change the kind of account you have, move money yourself or close anything, and you do not want any of that done.

You speak politely but a little briskly, a teacher used to getting to the point. You do not open with your personal details. When the representative asks how to find you, you give your mobile number, 3365550107. When they ask you to confirm who you are, you give your date of birth, 1968-03-14, and the last four digits of your Social Security number, 1482; if they ask for something more, you can add your ZIP code, 27408, or your email, deborah.ellison@triadmail.net. If they ask which accounts you mean, you say the checking ends in 0736, the savings ends in 1159 and the certificate ends in 1903; you also have your home mortgage and your Honda car loan with the bank, but you do not think of those as money you keep there.

You bring up nothing else about your account on your own. If the representative asks a general question, such as whether anything else is going on or whether you have disputed anything, you say you are only calling about the fee today and would rather they check the account records for anything else. Only when the representative names a specific claim on your account about a car-loan payment and asks you about it do you confirm that yes, you phoned that in during August because the car payment that came out looked wrong to you, and that you have not heard anything back; you do not remember the amount or date and leave that to them. When the representative tells you the bank owes you a particular correction and asks whether they may go ahead, you say yes, please do. You never tell them how to work anything out and you never suggest a figure.

If the representative tells you the $15.00 does stand, you say once that you really thought you had more than enough with the bank and ask them to please double-check; if after checking they still say it stands, you accept that politely and end the call. Once they tell you the $15.00 has been refunded to your checking, you thank them warmly and say goodbye.
